title: Listo Pairing Ledger
lede: A four-chassis template showing every field the format supports. The numbers here are illustrative, not a scored roster — copy this file, delete these chassis and author your own against listo-build/references/axis-rubrics.md. The pre-rebuild 26-chassis roster is archived beside this file as ledger-v1-roster.json; it predates the ten-axis model and will not validate.

Bombard.split: Profane Soul Blood Hunter 14 (INT) / Wizard 6 (Evocation), Wizard 1 first
Bombard.note: Wizard 1 grants Intelligence and Wisdom saves, the only clean route to a Wisdom save without spending Resilient. Brand of the Sapping Scar costs no concentration, which is why concentration is false here and why its control sits on the single-target axis — Brand_Castigation marks one creature.

Volley.note: Rogue 1 opens for the Dex + Int save pair, four skills and two Expertise. Ranger 11 buys Volley / Whirlwind — full weapon damage to every target, at-will, no save, no resource — which is the Act II AoE ceiling. Control stays low on both halves: this chassis answers crowds with damage, not with locks.

Zeal.note: Haste and Fireball sit on the domain list at Cleric 5 (Cleric Zeal Domain 5 = Target_Haste;Projectile_Fireball), and Consuming Fervor maximises Fire or Thunder twice per short rest. Holds Haste, so concentration is true — which caps its Saves at 3 in any act where Constitution is not proficient.

Vow.note: Paladin opens for heavy armour and Wis + Cha — neither repeatable by dipping later. Aura of Protection at Paladin 6 lands inside Act I and is a pair booster: it raises both bodies before the Personal min, and does not stack with a second aura.

Bombard.name: Bombard & Fervor
Bombard.verdict: The AoE moves onto the carry and is cast off the same Intelligence the chassis already maximises for Dark Augmentation and the Brand — so every DC lands into Brand of the Sapping Scar's blanket Disadvantage, which costs no concentration and therefore never competes with it.
Bombard.cost: Costs the 1d10 hemocraft die (BH 14 sits at 1d8 per the HemocraftDie levelmap), Action Surge, and the echo. Rescue is 0 on the carry, so the pair leans entirely on the support for it.

vars.note: Trades the maximised Fireball for an aura that lifts both bodies' saves.

vars.text: Wisdom variant: free prose, no numbers attached. The mod.io Hemocraft patch is not installed — check before scoring anything that assumes it.

Volley.name: Volley & Fervor
Volley.verdict: Volley is full weapon damage to every target with no save and no resource, delivered twice a round by Lone Wolf's second Action. That is the Act II AoE ceiling reached with a class feature rather than a slot.
Volley.cost: Control is thin on both axes, so the pair removes enemy action points by killing rather than locking — which is slower at +126% enemy HP than the raw damage suggests.

vars.note: Aura plus five proficient saves, at the price of the maximised burst.

cards.title: Tempo
cards.body: Damage and control both remove enemy action points — permanently and temporarily. Both are split crowd-versus-boss, blended by act, then capped by Actions: a capability you cannot afford to deploy delivers nothing.

cards.title: The rest
cards.body: Resilience (durability, saves, rescue), duration (endurance) and utility (skills) are weighted and averaged. Rescue sits here rather than in tempo because its action cost is already priced by where a chassis lands on the rubric ladder.

cards.title: Saves are derived
cards.body: Index 8 is always null. Author the proficient-ability set and any boosters; the renderer applies the rung table, the pair-scope aura rule, and the concentration cap.

caveats.h2: What would still move these numbers

assumptions.summary: Assumptions that would still move numbers
items: Every weight and half the fight-type coefficients are provisional. scoring-model.md §11 lists which constants are derived from a game mechanic and which are reasoned but uncalibrated. Do not cite a provisional number as evidence.
The 50/50 tempo split is deliberately neutral. The correlation that would justify moving it can only be computed on a roster that was not selected for being good at something.
Act bands are read off CombatExtender.json — Level.Bosses.Act caps boss level at 10 in Act I and 16 in Act II, identically across all three difficulty configs.
